terms.definition: Whoever sent an input; a multiplayer session has many.
Typed data attached to a session, an input or an event.
The six plugins that make an agent: settings, model, session, tools, context and loop.
The unit Liminal plugins are distributed in: an npm, git, or local package containing one or more plugins.
The point where the model rebuilds its context from memories, the entries no memory covers and its continuation note, so a session continues past the context window.
A slash command that runs on the agent side.
The set of plugins a host runs together, checked and built by compose.
What the model receives on a step: prompt sections plus history projected from the session log.
What the model writes at a checkpoint to carry on: the request and its limits, unfinished work, blockers, open questions and the next action.
What a plugin lets other plugins import: service tags, event kinds, attribute keys, schemas and slot handles.
The small mechanism that composes plugins: definePlugin, compose, registry, pipeline and attribute. It knows nothing about agents.
One of a plugin's export entries: contract, plugin, tui or web.
One entry in a session log, with a kind, data and attributes; its kind says whether the model sees it.
A registry, pipeline or attribute a contract exposes for other plugins to extend.
At a checkpoint, prompt sections that were only appended join the system prompt.
A way to see and drive sessions: the TUI, the desktop webview, print mode or a browser.
A new chat started from the current one, carrying context from it.
The program that runs a composition: the CLI, the desktop app, a web server or an embedding app.
Anything sent into a session: a user message, an answer, a notification, a cancel or a command.
Markdown rules an agent reads only when doing the work they cover.
A user, assistant or tool entry in model context, made of parts.
An LLM the agent calls, with known capabilities.
Which model a call uses, main or small, chosen in settings.
An event the model never sees.
A piece of a message: text, an image, reasoning, a tool call or a tool result.
An operation plugins wrap with middleware, such as a model call or a tool call.
One unit of behavior, built with definePlugin as an Effect layer, that adds to, wraps, attaches to or replaces other plugins.
The little face that murmurs words while a turn runs; plugins change his words and faces through moods.
The CLI running without the TUI, writing the reply or events to stdout.
Text a plugin contributes to every model request.
A plugin that supplies models from one vendor.
A list plugins add items to, such as tools, commands or event renderers.
The one process running a session's loop at a time.
One conversation with an agent, stored as an append-only log of events.
The plugin that stores session logs, such as in memory, SQLite or Postgres.
Frontend state folded from a session's events.
Configuration every plugin reads through Settings; plugins take no options of their own.
One plugin's block of settings, with a schema that holds its defaults.
A named screen region plugins fill from their tui and web entries.
One model call plus the tool calls it asks for. New input joins at the next step.
A named action the model can call, with an input schema.
One request from the model to run a tool, and its result.
A project folder whose own settings and bundles may load.
The loop's work from taking queued inputs until no tool owes a result and no new input arrived, ending with turn-end hooks.
